findings.claim: The trap tag on distractor A does not name the actual trap, and the taxonomy label that does fit sits on the untagged distractor D.
findings.evidence: Rationale: "A = outside_knowledge: the windowless hall means the light is artificial, so a reader may promote that incidental fact into the point" — the described mechanism is an inference from an IN-passage detail ('the hall has no windows'), not knowledge imported from outside. The same rationale describes D as "a plausible real-world belief (chemicals or minerals coloring the water) that the passage contradicts" and gives it no tag, yet that is verbatim the corpus definition of the tag: elf/families.json ELF-TYPE-001 trap_anatomy tag "outside_knowledge" — "First instinct is to fill in a story-shaped explanation ... a plausible real-world cause"; ELF-TYPE-006 layer1_distractor_patterns — "Rimlig verklig orsak som inte står i texten".
findings.why: The rationale is declared Layer-2 explanation source material (GENERATION.md: "This becomes Layer-2 explanation source material downstream") and the tags feed family-level trap statistics, so a swapped tag propagates a wrong misconception label to students and to the stats. Minor, not verdict-changing: both distractors are correctly ARGUED wrong in prose, only the taxonomy label is misplaced.

findings.claim: The world-knowledge shortcut that G-STEM flagged MAJOR is still present in the shipped file, and nothing in reviews/pedagogy.jsonl records that the pedagogy stage adjudicated it.
findings.evidence: verdicts.jsonl G-STEM q:1 verdict "flag", severity major: "WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick C): water is intrinsically blue through red-end absorption and the standard demonstration is exactly a white-lined indoor pool, so a reader who knows the physics picks C without the text." Independent re-test on options alone confirms it: A ("artificial lighting draws out a tint"), B ("a white lining brings out more color ... than a blue lining") and D ("comes from what is dissolved in the water") are all false as real-world physics, leaving C as the only factually true option — so a physics-literate student scores without reading. reviews/pedagogy.jsonl carries only {"verdict":"MINOR_FIXES"} with no findings field.
findings.why: Not a stage miss — the gate caught it and report.json carries the unit as SURVIVED_FLAGGED — so it does not refute the pedagogy verdict. Recorded here because the construct-validity risk ships with the unit and the accepted mitigation ("B and D are substantive real misconceptions ... normal comprehension work") lives only in the gate record, not in any review record.

findings.claim: "the hall" for the enclosure of an indoor municipal pool is the one lexical choice in the passage that leans Nordic/European rather than AmE, in a unit whose declared house style is AmE.
findings.evidence: Passage: "the municipal pool at Hallvik settles that question rather neatly: the hall has no windows". generator_meta.fictional_source.publication_type: "popular-science weekly, science desk column (AmE house style)"; spelling_variety "AmE". US copy for this referent is normally "the building", "the room", "indoor pool" or "natatorium"; "swimming hall" is a Scandinavian/German calque pattern (simhall, Schwimmhalle), and in AmE "pool hall" denotes billiards.
findings.why: Reported as an observation, not a defect: 'hall' = large room for assembly is dictionary-standard English, the setting is explicitly Nordic (Hallvik, Tova Ingelsson), and G-ENG passed 3-0 with G-REGISTER pass. It does not flip the language verdict (CORRECTED), but it is the item a native AmE desk editor would most plausibly still change.

findings.claim: The unit-level `family` slug uses the BrE spelling "colour" in a unit whose declared spelling_variety is AmE and whose own spelling_note asserts "no BrE spellings ('colour', 'metres')" are used.
findings.evidence: family: "ELF-TYPE-006 / swimming-pool-colour-water-absorption-optics-science-journalism-short" vs generator_meta.spelling_variety: "AmE". The spelling_note scopes its claim to "student-facing text", so the note is not false — but the metadata is internally inconsistent with the unit's declared variety.
findings.why: Cosmetic and non-student-facing, and there is precedent (elf-b1-001..004 batch: elf-b1-003 is AmE with "animal-behaviour-science-detail"). Flagged only because metadata/text cross-consistency is exactly what the integrated stage owns.

findings.claim: The three review records are verdict-only and identical for all seven units in the batch, so the recorded verdicts cannot be falsified from the records themselves.
findings.evidence: reviews/language.jsonl: all 7 lines "CORRECTED"; reviews/pedagogy.jsonl: all 7 lines "MINOR_FIXES"; reviews/integrated.jsonl: all 7 lines "MINOR_NOTES". No `findings` key on any line.
findings.why: I therefore audited the artifacts instead, and the artifacts DO substantiate each verdict for this unit: candidates→candidates-corrected shows the language edit ("the tiling gets the rest of it" → "the tiling gets the rest", passage and rationale in step), and candidates-corrected→candidates-final shows the pedagogy/integrated fixes — a rationale that had falsely claimed "every detail given about it strips one of them away" (untrue of 'the water is blue anyway') was rewritten to the correct three-way mapping, and a hedge_balance_note that had falsely claimed the key "carries no hedge marker; the distractors are unhedged too" was corrected to the accurate reading (C "can look blue", A "tends to"). Verdicts stand; only the record granularity is weak.
